## Attempt 3 complete — PR #132 is `fold-ready` at `115f12151c`

**Why attempt 2 didn't "not finish":** it did. It merged `1f7572a34c`, resolved both conflicts, pushed, and re-applied `fold-ready` — and the fold job handed the PR back again at 07:42Z because #136 folded under it. `$WORK/attempts/handback` reads 3 and cannot distinguish a dispatch from a failure. That's recorded at the top of `docs/lanes/handback/NOTES.md`, along with the observation that one more fold under this branch escalates the model and the one after opens a `decision-needed` issue about work that has been correct throughout.

**What this attempt did**

- Merged `origin/master` (through `912f58a1c1`). Moved the 42 checks into `docs/testing/jobs/selftest.d/99-handback.sh` unchanged; `selftest.sh` is now byte-identical to master's.
- **The move found a real defect in this PR's own fix.** `fold.sh` now calls `handback.sh` at the end of every tick, and `selftest.d/85-fold-ci.sh` drives the real `fold.sh` through a `gh` shim that answers *every* `pr list` with one fixed row. So every `fold_tick` also ran a handback tick, took that row at face value, and resumed `lane.foldci` and commented on #102 — three of that fragment's checks went red.

  The shim ignoring `--label` is a fixture artefact; trusting the filter was not. `handback.sh` asked for `--label needs-rebase` and never re-checked the rows carried it. The failure mode isn't an empty list — it's resuming, by name, whichever lane owns the first open PR, off that lane's four-attempt budget. A row returned for `--label X` without `X` is now refused and logged with the labels it did carry. `85-fold-ci.sh` is untouched.

| `jobs/` under test | whole suite | this fragment (46 checks) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this branch | **170 passed, 0 failed** | 46 / 46 |
| `origin/master` + only the fragment | 140 passed, **30 failed** | 16 / 46 |
| this branch, guard deleted | — | 40 / 46 |

The guard's check was written twice: with the fixture row labelled `harness,fold-ready`, two of its four checks passed against a guard-less build — the *stale-label* rule refused the row first and the guard did no work. Labelled `harness` alone, all four discriminate.

**Two caveats, stated rather than hidden**

- `preflight.sh --allow-tracker` fails only on the coverage gate (issue #138 has no lane), which reads `territory.toml`/`nv2a_issues.toml` from `origin/board` — files outside my 6-file diff. Not mine, not fixable from here.
- **CI is still building** (`jobs selftest`, Desktop, Android all in progress). I'm monitoring it; the local gate is green but the fold job gates on the GitHub verdict, so I'll report if anything goes red.

No handback has still been observed end-to-end on the real host — that limit was already in NOTES and this attempt didn't change it.
